First, we must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{x-2}{(x+8)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x+8}+\frac{B}{(x+8)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x+8)^{3}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x+8)^{3}$ and get

$$
x-2=A(x+8)^{2}+B(x+8)+C.
$$

Plugging in $x=-8,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(-8)-2 & =A(-8+8)^{2}+B(-8+8)+C \\ -10 & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=-7$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(-7)-2 & =A(-7+8)^{2}+B(-7+8)+C \\ -9 & =A+B-10 \\ A+B & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=-9$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(-9)-2 & =A(-9+8)^{2}+B(-9+8)+C \\ -11 & =A-B-10 \\ A-B & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations $A-B=-1$ and $A+B=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2A & =-1+1 \\ 2A & =0 \\ A & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

and substituting back into $A+B=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0+B & =1 \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum:

$$
\frac{x-2}{(x+8)^{3}}=\frac{1}{(x+8)^{2}}-\frac{10}{(x+8)^{3}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x-2}{(x+8)^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{(x+8)^{2}}-\frac{10}{(x+8)^{3}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{(x+8)^{2}}\,\text{d}x-10\int \frac{1}{(x+8)^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{x+8}+\frac{5}{(x+8)^{2}}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
